title: workload-profiling-prefetch-and-quant-scheduler
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: Customers with mixed workloads see suboptimal unit economics because static batching and cache defaults don't adapt to per-workload token distributions and model memory footprints. This PR implements a lightweight workload profiler, a cache-prefetch component, and a resource-aware quantization scheduler to reduce per-token cost while preserving tail-latency SLOs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a runtime workload fingerprinting agent that collects sequence length histograms, KV cache hit patterns, and transient concurrency spikes. The agent emits compact fingerprints once per minute for each model/route.
- Introduces a prefetcher that uses recent fingerprints to warm prefix/KV caches on cold-starty traffic patterns (short bursty queries that reuse prefixes). Prefetching is conservative by default and includes budget controls per-tenant.
- Implements a quantization scheduler that recommends per-model quant profiles (fp16, int8, mixed) based on memory headroom and observed latency sensitivity. Scheduler exposes a safe margin and cost/latency delta estimates.
- Exposes a new diagnostics endpoint and Console dashboard hooks to visualize model heatmaps, predicted cost delta, and prefetch budgets.

Design notes:
- Prefetch decisions are deterministic and weighted by an exponential moving average of prefix reuse probability; we avoid aggressive prefetch on low-score models.
- The quant scheduler simulates a latency/VRAM curve using offline microbenchmarks and live traces; recommendations are conservative (default margin +15% latency buffer).
- All components run in the serving control plane and are opt-in by route via a new config block (route.optimizations). This preserves per-customer control and avoids surprise behavior for managed Dedicated/Private installs.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for profiler aggregation and eviction logic.
- [x] Integration test that validates prefetch budget enforcement and does not increase 99th percentile latency by >5ms under synthetic burst load.
- [x] End-to-end A/B in perf-canary showed cost improvements for text-generation workloads.
- [x] Docs and Console wiring.

Benchmark summary (perf-canary results):
- Small generative assistant workload (avg seq=64): median cost per 1k tokens down 9.8%, median latency -6.1ms, 99th percentile latency +1.8ms (within SLO).
- Search-rewrite workload (avg seq=18 heavy prefix reuse): median cost per 1k tokens down 18.7% due to prefetch cache hits; 99th percentile latency -3.4ms.
- Mixed batch (spiky concurrency): overall cost down 7.2%, tail latency stable.

Rollout plan:

- Enable for 5% of hosted traffic for 48h with close monitoring of 99th percentile latencies and cost deltas.
- If metrics stable, escalate to 25%/50% then full rollout. Dedicated customers must opt-in via Console or API.
